statement: The typed triangle and its homogeneous spaces. Put $V=T_{\B}$, $D=T_{\dR}$ and $H=\operatorname{gr}_F D$. On the weight $n$ part, $\operatorname{gr}^p_F D$ is assigned bidegree $(p,n-p)$. Thus $T_{\mathrm{Hdg}}$ here means the associated-graded de Rham tensor fibre functor over $k$. The actual maps have types \[ \alpha:V_{\C}\longrightarrow D_{\C},\qquad \beta:D_{\C}\longrightarrow H_{\C},\qquad \gamma=(\beta\alpha)^{-1}:H_{\C}\longrightarrow V_{\C}. \] They are tensor isomorphisms; $\beta$ is the projection of each Hodge summand onto its associated-graded summand. Write \[ G=\Aut^\otimes(V),\quad G'=\Aut^\otimes(D),\quad B'=\Aut^\otimes(D,F),\quad U'=\ker\bigl(B'\longrightarrow\Aut^\otimes(H)\bigr). \] The normalized splitting space \[ Q=\{s:D\xrightarrow{\sim}H\text{ tensor and filtered}: \operatorname{gr}(s)=\id_H\} \] is a $U'$-torsor. Geometrically the filtration and bigrading spaces are $G/B$ and $G/L$, where $B$ and $L$ are the transported parabolic and Levi stabilizers. With $g=\dim G$, $b=\dim B$, $l=\dim L$, $u=\dim U$, one has \[ g=l+2u,\qquad b=l+u,\qquad g-b=u. \] The morphism $\BigSpace\to\Fil$ is a torsor under the relative unipotent group over $\Fil$ whose fibre at $F$ is $R_u(\operatorname{Stab}(F))$. Every fibre has dimension $u$.

statement: The $H'$ reading, the margin arrow, and the denominator. The two descriptions of $Q$ in P11 [I] are related by a precise normalization. If $H'$ is the inverse image in $B'$ of a nontrivial central one-dimensional torus $T_0=\im(j)$ in $B'/U'$, the enlarged splitting space $Q_H$ allowing $\operatorname{gr}(s)\in T_0$ is an $H'$-torsor. There is a morphism \[ Q_H\longrightarrow T_0,\qquad s\longmapsto\operatorname{gr}(s), \qquad Q=\text{fibre over }1. \] Consequently $\dim Q_H=u+1$ and $\dim Q=u$. After a splitting, $Q_H\simeq Q\times T_0$. If $j$ is an embedding, $T_0$ is the displayed $\Gm$; with a finite kernel the correct quotient is its image torus. The actual canonical $\beta$ lies in the normalized fibre $Q$. The natural parameter-space arrow is $\Phi\to F$, forgetting the grading. It induces an isomorphism on the discrete spaces of types; the inverse on types can have direction $F/G\to\Phi/G$. A $G$-equivariant section of the full parameter-space arrow exists only when $u=0$. For $G=\GL_2$ and a line filtration, even an arbitrary regular section is impossible. The lowercase-$k$ reading in P17 [I] gives the field extensions in the table below. The uppercase-$K$ reading of $\trdeg k(\alpha)/K$ or $\trdeg k(\beta)/K$ is undefined unless the numerator equals $K$, because $K=k(\alpha,\beta)$ contains both numerator fields; in that exceptional case the degree is zero.

statement: Algebraic extension and the conjugate comparison. Conjugation gives a rational tensor map $j_{\B}:V\to V_c$ and a $c$-semilinear map $j_{\dR}:D\to D_c$. In bases carried by $j_{\B}$ and $j_{\dR}$, the matrix of $\alpha_c$ is $\overline\alpha$.

statement: The exact unitary lift in the universal vector extension. Let $c=\pi/A$. The universal vector extension has the uniformization \[ E^\dagger(\C)=\C^2/\Lambda^\dagger,\qquad \Lambda^\dagger=\Z(\omega_1,\eta_1)+\Z(\omega_2,\eta_2). \] On its algebraic chart above $E\setminus\{O\}$, the coordinates and invariant differentials are \[ (u,s)\longmapsto(\wp(u),\wp'(u),t=\zeta(u)-s),\qquad du=dx/y,\quad ds=-dt-x\,dx/y. \] The canonical real Lie-group section $\kappa:E(\C)\to E^\dagger(\C)$, with image the maximal compact subgroup, is \[ \kappa([u])=[(u,hu+c\bar u)]. \] For every $P=[u]\in E(\Qb)\setminus\{O\}$, \[ t(\kappa(P))=\zeta(u)-hu-c\bar u\in\Qb \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P\text{ is torsion}. \] The complex-linear part of $d\kappa$ has image $L_h=\{s=hu\}\subset\operatorname{Lie}E^\dagger$. This line is defined over $\Qb$ exactly when $h$ is algebraic. Its annihilator $ds-hdu$ represents $-(\xi+h\omega)$ in de Rham cohomology.

statement: The restricted-Lie test for an algebraic splitting line. For every $a\in\Qb$, the line $L_a=\{s=au\}$ in $\operatorname{Lie}E^\dagger$ is not the Lie algebra of an algebraic subgroup. Its reductions therefore fail to be closed under $p$-th powers at infinitely many good primes of every number field of definition. In the preceding algebraic chart, put \[ D_a=y\partial_x+(6x^2-g_2/2)\partial_y-(x+a)\partial_t, \qquad V=-\partial_t. \] The derivation $D_a$ generates $L_a$. In characteristic five, \[ D_a^5=2g_2D_a+(3g_3-2g_2a)V. \] In particular, the actual CM example of A.4.4, with $(g_2,g_3,h)=(30,28,1/2)$, has good reduction at five and satisfies $D_h^5=4V$, which is not in the line generated by $D_h$.

statement: Torsion lifts and the exact horizontal-lift test. Write $Z(P)=\zeta(u)-hu-c\bar u$ for $P=[u]\ne O$. The addition and multiplication formulas are \[ Z(P+Q)=Z(P)+Z(Q)+\frac{y(P)-y(Q)}{2(x(P)-x(Q))}, \qquad Z(mP)=mZ(P)+R_m(P), \] where $R_m\in\Q(g_2,g_3)(E)$ is independent of $h$ and $c$, and the formulas hold wherever defined. For $P$ of exact order $n\ge2$, \[ Z(P)=-R_{n-1}(P)/n. \] In particular, $Z(P)=0$ at nonzero two-torsion, and \[ Z(P)=-\frac{12x(P)^2-g_2}{12y(P)} \] at nonzero three-torsion. For every algebraic $a$ and every nonzero algebraic point $P=[u]$, however, \[ \exp(L_a)\cap E^\dagger(\Qb)=\{O\},\qquad \zeta(u)-au\notin\Qb. \]

statement: The exact de Rham Hodge endomorphism algebra. Define \[ \mathcal D_E=\{T\in\operatorname{End}_{\Qb}H^1_{\dR}(E/\Qb): T_\C H^{1,0}\subset H^{1,0},\quad T_\C H^{0,1}\subset H^{0,1}\}. \] Writing $e=e_{\dR}$ as in A.4.11 gives the exact formula \[ \mathcal D_E =\{aI+(d-a)e:a,d\in\Qb,\ (d-a)h\in\Qb\}. \] Consequently $\mathcal D_E=\Qb I\oplus\Qb e\simeq\Qb\times\Qb$ when $h\in\Qb$, and $\mathcal D_E=\Qb I$ otherwise. The injective pullback map \[ \iota:\operatorname{End}_{\Qb}(E)\otimes_{\Z}\Qb \longrightarrow\mathcal D_E \] has precisely the image \[ \iota\bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\Qb}(E)\otimes\Qb\bigr) =\{T\in\mathcal D_E:T_B\in M_2(\Qb)\}. \] For CM curves this map is surjective. For a non-CM curve its image is $\Qb I$, so its cokernel has dimension one exactly when $h$ is algebraic. The Hodge projector $e_B$ itself is never rational over $\Q$, including in the CM case.

statement: Crystalline tests of the same projector, with coefficient fields retained. Let $E$ and a rank-one projector $e\in\operatorname{End}_L H^1_{\dR}(E/L)$ be defined over a number field $L$. Its crystalline-Frobenius fixity set cannot have lower weighted density greater than $3/4$, where the density is \[ \underline\delta(e)=\liminf_{X\to\infty} \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{v:\,p_v\le X\\\varphi_v(e)=e}} [L_v:\Q_{p_v}]\,\frac{\log p_v}{p_v-1}} {[L:\Q]\displaystyle\sum_{p\le X}\frac{\log p}{p-1}}. \] Finitely many ramified or bad-reduction places are omitted. In particular such a projector is never a $1$-absolute-Tate endomorphism. At an unramified good place, write $\varphi_v=F_v\sigma_v$, where $\sigma_v$ acts on the coefficients and $F_v=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. For $e=e_h=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&h\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ defined over $L$, the exact fixity test is \[ \varphi_v(e_h)=e_h \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C=0\quad\hbox{and}\quad A\sigma_v(h)+B=hD. \] For the CM curve $E:y^2=4x^3-30x-28$ and its $\Q$-defined projector $e_{1/2}$, this test fails at $p=5$.

statement: The exact denominator condition for an ordinary correction. Let $f(q)=\sum_{n\ge1}b(n)q^n$ be a normalized rational weight-two newform, let \[ \varepsilon(q)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{b(n)}n q^n, \qquad Z_a(q)=\zeta(\Lambda_f,\varepsilon(q))-a\varepsilon(q), \] and use the elliptic period lattice $\Lambda_f$ of Guerzhoy's construction. For every good ordinary prime outside its finite exceptional set there is $\lambda_p\in\Z_p$ such that, for every $a\in\C_p$, \[ \inf_n v_p([q^n]Z_a)>-\infty \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=\lambda_p. \] Algebraic coefficients do not, even in an actual CM splitting example, ensure bounded denominators. On \[ E_0:y^2=4x^3-4x,\qquad h(E_0)=0, \] put $t=-2x/y$ and let $u(t)$ be the formal logarithm with $du=dx/y$. Then \[ \zeta(u(t))=\frac1t-\frac12\sum_{n\ge1} \frac{(-1)^n\binom{2n}{n}}{4n-1}t^{4n-1}\in\Q((t)), \] and its coefficients have unbounded denominators at three. More precisely, for $n_r=(3^{2r+1}+1)/4$, the coefficient of $t^{3^{2r+1}}$ has valuation $-r-1$.

statement: The geometric mock-form coefficient is the same splitting scalar. Let $\pi:X_0(N)\to E$ be a modular parametrization over $\Q$, of degree $d$, with \[ \pi^*\omega=m\omega_f,\qquad \omega_f=f(q)\frac{dq}{q},\qquad m\in\Q^\times, \] for a normalized rational newform $f$. In its two-dimensional de Rham component choose \[ \eta_f^{\rm alg}=\frac m d\pi^*\xi. \] This class is cup-dual to $\omega_f$. The complex number $a$ defined by Candelori's decomposition \[ \eta_f^{\rm alg}=a\omega_f+b\overline{\omega_f} \] satisfies the exact identity \[ a=-\frac{m^2}{d}h(E). \] For the weight-zero harmonic Maass form constructed from this class, with algebraic constant term, all of its holomorphic coefficients are algebraic exactly when $h(E)$ is algebraic. With a rational constant term, their field is precisely $\Q(h(E))$.

statement: The weight-two overconvergent criterion and its exact remaining equation. Let $f$ be the rational weight-two newform of an elliptic curve $E/\Q$, and let $p\ge5$ be a good ordinary prime. Write \[ T^2-b(p)T+p=(T-\beta)(T-\beta'),\qquad v_p(\beta)=0,\quad v_p(\beta')=1, \] and let $V(f)(q)=f(q^p)$ and $\theta=q\,d/dq$. Under the identification of the $f$-component with $H^1_{\dR}(E/\Q_p)$, the following three conditions are equivalent: \[ E\text{ has CM};\qquad f-\beta V(f)\in\operatorname{im}\theta;\qquad \Phi(\operatorname{Fil}^1)=\operatorname{Fil}^1. \] Here the image of $\theta$ is taken in the overconvergent spaces on the wide-open ordinary locus used in \cite[Theorem 3.3]{EllCandeloriCastella2017}, and $\Phi$ is crystalline Frobenius. For a non-CM $E$, let $r$ be a weakly holomorphic weight-two form with zero residues whose class $\delta$ belongs to the $f$-component. Let $B(q)$ be its formal primitive, $\theta B=r$, and put $\varepsilon=\sum b(n)q^n/n$. There is a unique $\alpha\in\C_p$ for which \[ (B-\alpha\varepsilon)\bigm|\left(1-\frac{\beta'}pV\right) \] is overconvergent. It is characterized exactly by \[ (1-\Phi/\beta)(\delta-\alpha[f])=0. \] In particular, $\alpha=0$ precisely when $\delta$ belongs to the unit-root Frobenius line.

statement: The exact defect between the complex and ordinary differential operators. On a fine modular curve, work locally with an algebraic symplectic frame $(\omega,\xi)$ of the universal elliptic de Rham bundle, with $\omega$ spanning the Hodge line and $\langle\omega,\xi\rangle=1$. Write \[ \nabla\omega=\omega\otimes A+\xi\otimes B, \qquad \operatorname{KS}(\omega^{\otimes2})=B. \] Here $B$ is a local generator of the cotangent bundle. Projection along the complement $L_a=\langle\xi+a\omega\rangle$, followed by Kodaira--Spencer, defines the weight-raising operator \[ D_a(f\omega^{\otimes k}) =\left(\frac{df}{B}+k\left(\frac AB-a\right)f\right) \omega^{\otimes(k+2)}. \] For any two complements, \[ (D_a-D_b)(f\omega^{\otimes k}) =k(b-a)f\omega^{\otimes(k+2)}. \] At a good ordinary point, let $L_{u_p}$ be the unit-root complement. For a specified embedding into $\C_p$ of a number field containing an algebraic $h$, agreement of the two operators on one section of nonzero weight and nonzero value is exactly $\iota_p(h)=u_p$.

statement: The reduced theta coefficient field and its torsion translations. Let $k=\Q(g_2,g_3)$ for the fixed short Weierstrass equation, let $\sigma(u)$ be normalized by $\sigma'(0)=1$, and let $h$ be the actual Hodge splitting coefficient. The normalized reduced theta function and the associated Kronecker theta function are \[ \theta_h(u)=e^{-hu^2/2}\sigma(u),\qquad \Theta_h(u,v)=e^{-huv}\frac{\sigma(u+v)}{\sigma(u)\sigma(v)}. \] Their Taylor or Laurent coefficient fields over $k$ are exactly $k(h)$. Under the principal polarization, $\Theta_h$ represents the canonical meromorphic section of \[ m^*\mathcal O_E([0])\otimes p_1^*\mathcal O_E([0])^{-1}\otimes p_2^*\mathcal O_E([0])^{-1} \quad\hbox{on }E\times E. \] For every nonzero torsion point represented by $u_0\in\Lambda\otimes\Q$, the reduced translation \[ T_{u_0}(u)= e^{-c\bar u_0(u+u_0/2)}\theta_h(u+u_0), \qquad c=\frac{\pi}{\operatorname{Area}(\Lambda)}, \] has coefficient field over $\Qb$ exactly $\Qb(h)$.

statement: The exact G-function input for the elliptic primitive. Let $K$ be a number field, let $E:y^2=P(x)=4x^3-g_2x-g_3$ be smooth over $K$, and let $Q=(x_0,y_0)\in E(K)$ satisfy $y_0\ne0$. For every $a\in K$, the germ \[ F_a(t)=-\int_0^t\frac{x_0+s+a}{\sqrt{P(x_0+s)}}\,ds, \qquad \sqrt{P(x_0)}=y_0, \] is a $G$-function over $K$. In the coordinate $x=x_0+t$ it satisfies \[ 2P(x)(x+a)F_a''+ \bigl(P'(x)(x+a)-2P(x)\bigr)F_a'=0. \] For some integer $C\ge1$, the first $n$ Taylor coefficients have a common denominator dividing \[ (4C)^{n+1}\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n). \] If $x=\wp(u)$ and $x_0=\wp(u_0)$, the exact analytic expression is \[ F_a(x-x_0)=\zeta(u)-au-\zeta(u_0)+au_0. \] At $a=h$, its additive monodromy along an elliptic loop of period $\lambda$ is $c\bar\lambda$, and is nonzero whenever $\lambda\ne0$.

statement: Horizontal Hodge jets and an explicit CM denominator obstruction. In the Legendre family \[ E_t:y^2=4x(x-1)(x-t),\qquad \omega=dx/y,\quad \eta=x\,dx/y, \] the Gauss--Manin connection matrix, with columns giving the derivatives of the basis, is \[ C(t)=\begin{pmatrix}A&A\\ B&-A\end{pmatrix},\qquad A=\frac1{2(1-t)},\qquad B=-\frac1{2t(1-t)}. \] At $t_0=1/2$, the antiholomorphic class is $\eta-\omega/2$, and the short Weierstrass equation has $g_2=1$, $g_3=0$, and $h=0$. Its horizontal extension $F(s)\omega+G(s)\eta$, with $s=t-1/2$, is \[ G(s)=\sum_{m\ge0} \frac{\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(4j+1)^2}{(2m)!}s^{2m}, \qquad F(s)=\left(\frac12-2s^2\right)G'(s) -\left(\frac12+s\right)G(s). \] For every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$, the coefficient $[s^{p+1}]G$ has $p$-adic valuation $-1$. Thus this actual algebraic CM Hodge splitting has horizontal Taylor coefficients with infinitely many denominator primes, and fails the $\omega(p)$-integrality condition of Lam--Litt. More generally, at every algebraic nonsingular Legendre parameter and every nonzero algebraic initial vector in a positive symmetric power of its de Rham cohomology, the horizontal extension fails both integrality conditions of \cite[Theorem 4.1.1, p.21]{EllLamLitt2025}.

statement: Division-polynomial data preserve the Gaussian parameter ambiguity. For any $a\in\C$, put $\theta_a(u)=e^{-au^2/2}\sigma(u)$ and $\eta^{(a)}_\lambda=\eta_\lambda-a\lambda$. The normalized division polynomial $F_n$ satisfies \[ F_n(\wp(u),\wp'(u)) =\frac{\sigma(nu)}{\sigma(u)^{n^2}} =\frac{\theta_a(nu)}{\theta_a(u)^{n^2}}. \] For every $u_0\in\Lambda\otimes\Q$, the normalized torsion constant likewise satisfies \[ e^{-\eta^{(a)}_{u_0}u_0/2}\theta_a(u_0) =e^{-\eta_{u_0}u_0/2}\sigma(u_0). \] Thus the map from the parameter $a$ to all division-polynomial quotients and these torsion constants is constant. The same quotient identities hold as formal series over every characteristic-zero coefficient field, including a $p$-adic field.

statement: The Hodge parameter uniquely minimizes the quadratic growth type. Let $c=\pi/\operatorname{area}(\Lambda)>0$ and, for $a\in\C$, put \[ \theta_a(u)=e^{-au^2/2}\sigma(u),\qquad M_a(r)=\max_{|u|\le r}|\theta_a(u)|. \] Then \[ \log M_a(r)=\frac{c+|h-a|}{2}\,r^2+O(r) \qquad(r\longrightarrow+\infty). \] In particular, every $\theta_a$ has order two, its quadratic type is $(c+|h-a|)/2$, and $a=h$ is the unique parameter of minimal type. This gives an exact analytic property specific to the actual Hodge parameter, in addition to the coefficient-field identity in A.4.26.

statement: The corrected elliptic vector field at every good prime. Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>3$, and let \[ E/k:\quad y^2=P(x)=4x^3-g_2x-g_3 \] be smooth. Define the two explicit coefficients \[ H_p=[x^{p-1}]P(x)^{(p-1)/2},\qquad K_p=[x^{p-2}]P(x)^{(p-1)/2}. \] In the rational universal-extension chart of A.4.14, for $a\in k$ put \[ D_a=y\partial_x+ \left(6x^2-\frac{g_2}{2}\right)\partial_y -(x+a)\partial_t,\qquad V=-\partial_t. \] The restricted $p$-th power, defined by the $p$-fold iterate of a derivation, is \[ \boxed{\quad D_a^p=H_pD_a-(K_p+aH_p)V.\quad} \] Consequently the line $kD_a$ is stable under restricted $p$-th power exactly when $K_p+aH_p=0$. In ordinary reduction this determines the unique value $a=-K_p/H_p$. In supersingular reduction no line $kD_a$ is stable under restricted $p$-th power.

statement: A density bound for the explicit restricted-Lie congruences. Let $K$ contain $g_2,g_3,a$, where $a$ is algebraic and $E:y^2=4x^3-g_2x-g_3$ is smooth, and put $d=[K:\Q]$. Omit finitely many primes so that all data have good integral reduction and their residue characteristics exceed three. For a prime $v$ of $K$ above the rational prime $p$, put \[ w_v=[K_v:\Q_p]\frac{\log p}{p-1},\qquad \beta_K(a)=\liminf_{R\to\infty} \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{v\mid p,\ p\le R\\ K_p+aH_p=0\ {\rm in}\ k(v)}}w_v} {\displaystyle\sum_{v\mid p,\ p\le R}w_v}. \] Here $H_p,K_p$ are the reductions of the coefficients in A.4.31. Then \[ \boxed{\qquad \beta_K(a)\le 1-\frac1{4d}.\qquad} \] In particular, the bound over $\Q$ is $3/4$. Equivalently, the complementary weighted upper density is at least $1/(4d)$. The analytic input is uniform in the correction parameter: the curve $\Theta_a(u)=\exp(u,au)$ has an order-two uniformization in an explicit projective compactification. For the ample bundle constructed below, the least quadratic type of a nonzero holomorphic growth section is $Nc/2$ for every $a$, where $c=\pi/\operatorname{area}(\Lambda)$.

statement: The conjugate elliptic quotient and its differential scalar. Let $E/\Qb$, $h$, and $c=\pi/\operatorname{area}(\Lambda)>0$ have the preceding normalizations. The algebraic conjugate curve $\overline E$ has differential-normalized lattice $\bar\Lambda$. There is a surjective analytic group homomorphism \[ \Phi_h:E^\dagger(\C)\longrightarrow\overline E(\C), \qquad [(u,s)]\longmapsto[(s-hu)/c]\pmod{\bar\Lambda}. \] Its kernel is $\exp(L_h)$, and $u\mapsto[(u,hu)]$ is an injective uniformization of that kernel. On the maximal compact subgroup, it satisfies $\Phi_h(\kappa([u]))=[\bar u]$. The homomorphism $\Phi_h$ is never algebraic over $\C$. Writing $v$ for the holomorphic uniformizing coordinate of $\overline E$, its differential is \[ \Phi_h^*(dv)=c^{-1}(ds-h\,du), \qquad d\Phi_h=(-h/c,\ 1/c) \] in the algebraic coordinates of A.4.14. The pair $(h,c)$ cannot belong to $\Qb^2$. In particular, whenever $h$ is algebraic, $c$ is transcendental. For the actual CM example $(g_2,g_3,h)=(30,28,1/2)$, $\Phi_h$ is consequently an explicit nonalgebraic analytic homomorphism between algebraic groups whose differential has algebraic projective class $[-1/2:1]$.

statement: The exact quotient lattice and its CM case. Let $E/\Qb$, $\omega_i,\eta_i,h,c,A$ have the conventions of A.4.1, and put \[ \mu_i(a)=\eta_i-a\omega_i,\qquad \Lambda_a=\Z\mu_1(a)+\Z\mu_2(a). \] For $a\in\C$, this is a full lattice in $\C$ exactly when $|h-a|\ne c$. Off that circle its basis ratio satisfies \[ r_a=\frac{\eta_2-a\omega_2}{\eta_1-a\omega_1}, \qquad \operatorname{Im}r_a =\frac{A\bigl(|h-a|^2-c^2\bigr)} {|\eta_1-a\omega_1|^2}. \] There is a holomorphic map \[ F_a:E(\C)\setminus\{O\}\longrightarrow \C/\Lambda_a, \qquad [u]\longmapsto[\zeta(u)-au], \qquad F_a^*(dz)=-(x+a)\omega. \] It has no holomorphic extension at $O$ and is not algebraic. For algebraic $a$ and a full lattice $\Lambda_a$, the complex elliptic curve $\C/\Lambda_a$ has CM if and only if $E$ has CM and $a=h$.

statement: Symmetric-square tensor and conjugate-extension map. For a real algebraic short model with three real roots, choose $\omega_1=w>0$ and $\omega_2=\tau w\in i\mathbf R_{>0}$. Put \[ T_a=\begin{pmatrix}2a&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad P=\begin{pmatrix}w&-(h+c)w\\ \tau w&-(h-c)\tau w\end{pmatrix}. \] The actual K\"unneth class \[ \theta_a=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega\wedge\operatorname{pr}_2^*\xi +\operatorname{pr}_1^*\xi\wedge\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega +2a\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega\wedge\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega \] has product-cycle period matrix $PT_aP^{\mathsf T}$, and \[ \frac{PT_aP^{\mathsf T}}{2\pi i} =\begin{pmatrix} (a-h-c)/(c\tau)&(a-h)/c\\ (a-h)/c&(a-h+c)\tau/c \end{pmatrix}. \] At $a=h$ this matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(-\tau^{-1},\tau)$. For a non-CM curve no nonzero complex scalar multiple of this Betti vector has all coordinates algebraic. The determinant-twisted symmetric-square comparison identifies this class with the earlier Hodge projector by an explicit isomorphism. For every algebraic short model, without the reality restriction, the unique complex-linear map carrying its universal-extension period basis to the conjugate period basis is \[ M=\begin{pmatrix} -h/c&1/c\\ c-h\bar h/c&\bar h/c \end{pmatrix}. \] It descends to a holomorphic group isomorphism $(E^\dagger)^{\mathrm{an}}\to(\bar E^\dagger)^{\mathrm{an}}$, with $\det M=-1$ and $\bar M M=I$. This map is not algebraic; its entries cannot all be algebraic.

statement: Integral tangent, isogeny law, and branch denominators. At a place of good ordinary reduction of residue characteristic $p>3$, the inverse-Verschiebung construction gives an integral line in $\operatorname{Lie}E^\dagger$ projecting isomorphically to $\operatorname{Lie}E$. Write its slope as $\upsilon_p(E)$ in the algebraic coframe $(du,ds)$ of A.4.14 and a good short N\'eron frame. It is functorial under actual isogenies. For a finite subgroup $C$ of order $N$, put $S_C=\sum_{P\in C\setminus\{0\}}x(P)$, and let $f:E\to E'$ be its quotient, with $f^*\omega'=\lambda\omega$. In short frames, \[ \lambda^2h(E')=Nh(E)+S_C,\qquad \lambda^2\upsilon_p(E')=N\upsilon_p(E)+S_C. \] For $h\in\Qb$, fix an embedding of a number field containing $h$ and the isogeny data into $\mathbf C_p$. In that field, \begin{equation}\label{ell:ordinary-isogeny-difference} \lambda^2\bigl(h(E')-\upsilon_p(E')\bigr) =N\bigl(h(E)-\upsilon_p(E)\bigr). \end{equation} For every number field $K$ containing $g_2,g_3,h$, the actual Hodge coefficients in differential-preserving quotient frames satisfy $\sigma(h(E_C))=h(E_{\sigma C})$ for $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\Qb/K)$. Normalize $v_p(p)=1$. Suppose $h$ is integral at the chosen place and $h\ne\upsilon_p(E)$, and put $b=v_p(h-\upsilon_p(E))\ge0$. Among cyclic subgroups of order $p^n$, let $m$ be the logarithm to base $p$ of the order of the intersection with multiplicative torsion. Then, in good N\'eron frames on their targets, \[ v_p(\lambda_C)=m,\qquad d_p(C):=\max\{0,-v_p(h(E_C))\}=\max\{0,2m-n-b\}. \] There are respectively \[ p^n\ (m=0),\qquad (p-1)p^{n-m-1}\ (1\le m<n),\qquad 1\ (m=n) \] such subgroups; their total is $D_n=(p+1)p^{n-1}$. The sum of $d_p(C)$ is at most $S_n$, where \[ S_{2r}=\frac{2(p^r-1)}{p-1},\qquad S_{2r+1}=\frac{(p+1)p^r-2}{p-1}. \] For non-CM $E$, every actual $\operatorname{Gal}(\Qb/K)$-orbit $\mathcal O$ of these subgroups satisfies \[ \frac1{|\mathcal O|}\sum_{C\in\mathcal O}d_p(C) \le I_p\frac{S_n}{D_n}=O_{E,K,p}(p^{-n/2}), \] where $I_p=[\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbf Z_p):\rho_p(\operatorname{Gal}(\Qb/K))]$.

statement: Two normalized jets of the period product. statement: Exact local sizes and arithmetic type of the invariant leaf. Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve in the algebraic normalization of A.4.14, let $a\in K$, and write $d=[K:\Q]$. In its universal vector extension $G=E^\dagger$, let $\widehat C_a$ be the formal leaf at the identity of the invariant line $L_a=\{s=au\}$. Choose, once over $K$, \'etale parameters $X,Y$ at the identity such that \[ X(e)=Y(e)=0,\qquad D_aX(e)=1,\qquad D_aY(e)=0. \tag{A.4.40a} \] Write the actual formal graph as $Y=\phi_a(X)=\sum_{n\ge2}b_nX^n\in K[[X]]$. Outside a finite set of places, put \[ \mathcal B_a=\{v:K_{p_v}+aH_{p_v}\ne0\pmod v\},\qquad d_v=[K_v:\Q_{p_v}]. \] For the absolute value normalized by $\|p\|_v=p^{-d_v}$, the geometric size of this precise embedded formal curve satisfies \[ S_v(\widehat C_a)=\|p\|_v^{1/(p-1)}\quad(v\in\mathcal B_a), \qquad S_v(\widehat C_a)\ge\|p\|_v^{1/(p(p-1))} \quad(v\notin\mathcal B_a). \tag{A.4.40b} \] Consequently its adelic size product is zero. In particular this formal leaf fails the A-analyticity condition in Bost--Chambert-Loir's Definition~3.7. For Andr\'e's normalization $|p|_v=p^{-d_v/d}$ and his arithmetic coefficient invariant $\tau$, the same fixed graph satisfies \[ \tau(\phi_a)\ \ge\ \limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac1T \sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal B_a\\p_v\le T}} \frac{d_v}{d}\log p_v \ \ge\ \frac1{4d}>0. \tag{A.4.40c} \] Thus the zero-$\tau$ hypothesis of Andr\'e's Theorem~5.4.3 fails for this actual graph. statement: A profinite loop with integral classes on every finite cover. statement: The completion preserved by all affine integral homology maps. Let \(F=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle\) be a specified discrete free group of finite rank, and put \(G=\widehat F\). For each open normal subgroup \(N\subset G\), set \[ \begin{aligned} K_N&=F\cap N,& A_N&=K_N/[K_N,K_N],\\ D_N&=\overline{[K_N,K_N]}^{\,G},& \Gamma_N&=F/[K_N,K_N],\\ P_N&=G/D_N,& Q_N&=G/N=F/K_N. \end{aligned} \tag{E.2.28a} \] The group \(\Gamma_N\) embeds in \(P_N\). Define the actual subgroup and its displayed inverse-limit realization by \[ \mathcal H_{\mathrm{int}} =\bigcap_N\pi_N^{-1}(\Gamma_N)\subset G, \qquad \mathcal H_{\mathrm{int}}\simeq\varprojlim_N\Gamma_N, \quad \pi_N:G\longrightarrow P_N. \tag{E.2.28b} \] For an open subgroup \(U\subset G\), write \(\Lambda_U=(F\cap U)^{\mathrm{ab}}\subset U^{\mathrm{ab}}\). This is the integral homology lattice of its actual finite cover of the bouquet of \(r\) circles. For a continuous automorphism \(\alpha\) of \(G\), the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The actual induced map \(U^{\mathrm{ab}}\to \alpha(U)^{\mathrm{ab}}\) carries \(\Lambda_U\) onto \(\Lambda_{\alpha(U)}\) for every open \(U\). \item The same assertion holds on the integral lattices \(A_N\) for one characteristic cofinal chain of open normal subgroups. \item There is one element \(h\in G\) such that \((\operatorname{ad}(h)\alpha)(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{int}}) =\mathcal H_{\mathrm{int}}\). \end{enumerate} Furthermore, an actual continuous automorphism \(\beta\) of \(G\) preserves \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{int}}\) if and only if \(\beta(x_j)\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{int}}\) for \(1\leq j\leq r\). For the punctured curve of E.2.22 this characterizes preservation of all \emph{affine} integral homology lattices, up to one actual inner adjustment. Passing from the proper-homology condition in E.2.22 to this affine condition requires the vanishing of the boundary-extension classes identified below. statement: An integral IA lift that moves actual boundary homology. statement: The embedded completion determined by all proper cover lattices. Let \(F=\langle x,y\rangle\) be the specified topological fundamental group of \(X=\mathbf P^1(\C)\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\), put \(z=(xy)^{-1}\), and put \(G=\widehat F\). statement: The fourfold numerical quotient and its actual correspondence scope. Let \(k\) be a field, let \(\ell\) be a prime invertible in \(k\), and use rational algebraic cycles and geometric \(\ell\)-adic cohomology. For every abelian variety \(A/k\) of dimension at most four, the identity on cycles gives an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{CH}^r(A)_{\Q}/{\sim_\ell} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{CH}^r(A)_{\Q}/{\sim_{\rm num}} \qquad(r\in\Z). \tag{F.3.35a} \] In the contravariant convention for pure motives, the numerical quotient is therefore fully faithful on the additive categories with split idempotents generated by \(h(A)(m)\), where \(\dim A\leq2\) and \(m\in\Z\). Its image contains every numerical direct summand of a finite direct sum of those generators. For a finite field \(k\) and a fourfold \(A/k\), the cycle map \[ \operatorname{CH}^2(A)\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow H^4_{\acute{e}t} (A_{\overline k},\Q_\ell(2))^{G_k} \tag{F.3.35b} \] is surjective. These assertions retain the source's fourfold dimension bound; the general numerical-quotient obligation in F.3.5 and the fixed Betti comparison in E.2 remain on the page.
